1.1: Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy, our brother, To Philemon, our beloved friend and fellow worker,
1.2: To the beloved Apphia, Archippus, our fellow soldier, and to the church in your house:
1.3: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.4: I thank God and always mention you in my prayers,
1.5: I've been hearing about your love and faith, how you show it towards the Lord Jesus and towards all the saints,
1.6: That your sharing of your faith might become powerful by recognizing all the good things in you, in Christ Jesus.
1.7: We're overjoyed and comforted by your love, because you've refreshed the hearts of the saints, brother.
1.8: Even though I could be bold in Christ and tell you what to do,
1.9: For the sake of love, I'd rather ask you instead—me, Paul, the old man, and now also a prisoner for Jesus Christ—
1.10: I'm asking you for my son, Onesimus, whom I became a father to while locked up,
1.11: Who was once useless to you, but now he's useful to both you and me.
1.12: I'm sending him back to you, but really, he's like my own heart.
1.13: I wanted to keep him here with me so he could help me while I'm in these chains for the gospel,
1.14: But I didn't want to do anything without your consent, so your good deed wouldn't be forced, but done willingly.
1.15: Maybe he left you for a while just so you could receive him back forever,
1.16: Not just as a servant, but more than that—a beloved brother. Especially to me, but how much more to you, both in the flesh and in the Lord.
1.17: So, if you count me as a partner, receive him as you would me.
1.18: But if he's done you wrong or owes you anything, charge it to me.
1.19: I, Paul, am writing this with my own hand—I'll pay it back, not to mention, you owe me your own self, too.
1.20: Yes, brother, let me have joy from you in the Lord; refresh my heart in the Lord.
1.21: I'm confident you'll obey me, and I know you'll even do more than what I ask.
1.22: And while you're at it, prepare a guest room for me, 'cause I'm trusting that through your prayers, I'll be granted to come see you.
1.23: Epaphras, my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, sends his greetings,
1.24: As do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellow workers.
1.25: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
